symptoms: throbbing headache on one side of the head, nausea, vomiting, sensitivity to light (photophobia), sensitivity to sound, visual aura
guidance: Rest in a quiet, dark room. Stay hydrated and use a cool compress on the forehead. Over-the-counter pain relievers may help if taken early. Consult a doctor if migraines occur frequently or worsen.

symptoms: dull, aching head pain, tightness or pressure across the forehead or on the sides and back of the head, tenderness in scalp and neck muscles, no nausea or vomiting
guidance: Practice stress management, apply a warm heating pad to neck muscles, ensure adequate hydration and sleep, and consider mild analgesics if needed.

source: CDC Clinical Care Guidance - Acute Respiratory Illnesses
symptoms: runny or stuffy nose, sore throat, mild cough, sneezing, mild fatigue, low-grade fever
guidance: Get plenty of rest, drink warm fluids, use saline nasal sprays, and gargle with warm salt water for throat relief. Antibiotics are not effective against viral infections.

symptoms: sudden onset high fever, severe body aches, muscle pain, chills, dry cough, profound fatigue, headache
guidance: Isolate to prevent spread, prioritize rest and oral hydration. High-risk individuals or those within 48 hours of symptom onset should consult a physician for antiviral evaluation.

symptoms: watery diarrhea, abdominal cramps, nausea, occasional vomiting, low-grade fever after eating or contact with sick individuals
guidance: Focus on oral rehydration solutions (ORS) with electrolytes. Eat bland foods (bananas, rice, toast) once vomiting subsides. Seek care if unable to keep liquids down for 24 hours.

symptoms: itchy watery eyes, sneezing fits, clear runny nose, nasal congestion, itchy throat or roof of mouth, triggered by dust, pollen, or pet dander without fever
guidance: Minimize exposure to known allergens, use saline nasal rinses, and consider non-drowsy over-the-counter antihistamines or corticosteroid nasal sprays.

source: NIDDK - Acid Reflux & GERD Clinical Guide
symptoms: burning sensation in the upper stomach or lower chest after eating (heartburn), sour taste in mouth, regurgitation of food or liquid, worse when lying down
guidance: Avoid spicy, fatty, or acidic meals late at night, eat smaller portions, elevate the head of your bed, and consider antacids. See a doctor if symptoms occur more than twice a week.
